title: Marketplace positioning snippets (scratchpad) — AWS/GCP listing refresh
content:
NOTE: This is a scratchpad. Fragments + alternates. Not all statements are cleared by Security/Legal. Use for brainstorming only.

==============================
0) Goal of this doc
==============================
Collect punchy phrases for AWS/GCP Marketplace listings + sales enablement that:
- Preserve dev-first vibe but address enterprise procurement/security checkboxes
- Make “inference serving” differentiation legible (latency/cost/reliability + deployment flexibility)
- Avoid over-claiming on compliance (SOC2/ISO wording must be exact; security packet controls must match)

Open questions to resolve elsewhere:
- Exact SKU names and what’s included vs add-on (retention/compliance/premium SLA)
- Whether to position “Hosted API” vs “Dedicated” vs “Private” as separate listings or within one listing + plans (GCP might prefer fewer offers?)

==============================
1) One-liners / headline candidates
==============================
A) Plain, procurement-friendly
- “Production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency, cost, and uptime.”
- “Enterprise-ready LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”
- “Run open models in production with performance you can measure.”

B) Dev-first
- “Ship LLM features faster—without owning the serving stack.”
- “A unified inference runtime for hosted + private deployments.”
- “Low-latency LLM inference you can actually operate.”

C) Marketplace-specific (procurement angle)
- “Buy Redwood Inference through AWS/GCP Marketplace and apply spend to your cloud commit.”
- “Simplify procurement for LLM inference: marketplace billing + enterprise controls.”

D) Differentiation-forward (careful to keep honest)
- “Optimize inference economics with batching, caching, routing, and observability built in.”
- “Serving-first platform: cost/latency controls + rollout safety for model versions.”

==============================
2) Value prop blocks (mix + match)
==============================
Block 1: Performance + economics
- “High-throughput inference runtime tuned for real production traffic.”
- “Continuous batching and cache-aware execution to reduce per-token cost while protecting latency.”
- “Policy-based routing and graceful fallback to keep applications online during demand spikes.”

Alt phrasing:
- “Lower unit cost without guessing: token-level cost + latency breakdowns and operational levers.”
- “Make LLM serving predictable: stable p95 latency, controllable spend, and clear SLOs.”

Block 2: Deployment flexibility
- “Same API and operational tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).”
- “Pin model versions, control rollouts, and standardize inference across teams/environments.”

Alt phrasing:
- “Start hosted; move to dedicated or private when security, scale, or isolation requires—without rewriting your app.”

Block 3: Operability + safety
- “Observability built for inference: per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis.”
- “Canary deploys and A/B tests for model versions; automatic fallback policies.”

Alt phrasing:
- “Treat models like prod services: versioning, safe rollouts, and regression detection tied to eval sets.”

Block 4: Enterprise checkboxes (DO NOT over-claim)
- “Security and compliance documentation available for enterprise buyers.”
- “Encryption and audit logging details provided in the security packet.”

WIP phrasing that needs Sec review before use:
- “Customer data isolation options via dedicated capacity and private deployments.”
- “Customer-managed key integration options (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments.”

==============================
3) What we are / what we are not (positioning anchors)
==============================
- We are not “just a model catalog.” We’re a serving + operations platform.
- We are not “DIY GPU hosting.” We provide a consistent runtime, routing, observability, and rollout tooling.
- We’re not “one environment only.” We support hosted + dedicated + private.

Suggested sentence:
- “Redwood is the layer between your app and the rapidly changing model/hardware landscape—so you can optimize performance without replatforming.”

==============================
4) Competitive callouts (soft, avoid naming)
==============================
Against general LLM APIs:
- “More control over latency/cost tradeoffs, rollouts, and deployment isolation.”
- “More transparency: measurable performance + operational tooling for production traffic.”
- “More flexibility: deploy hosted today; shift to dedicated/private later.”

Against cloud ‘model endpoints’ / generic managed inference:
- “Serving features designed for LLM workloads: batching, KV/prefix caching, fallback routing.”
- “Unified developer experience across environments (not tied to a single deployment mode).”

Against self-hosted open-source runtimes:
- “Less operational burden: managed routing, monitoring, and enterprise onboarding.”
- “Procurement-friendly: marketplace purchase + entitlements mapped to orgs/environments.”

==============================
5) Proof / credibility snippets (use carefully)
==============================
Things that are generally safe if accurate:
- “Built for production reliability (monitoring, alerts, retries, and controlled rollouts).”
- “Designed to support regulated workflows with private networking options and audit logging capabilities.”

Things to avoid unless verified in security packet language:
- “HIPAA compliant” / “FedRAMP” / “ISO certified” (unless exact current status + scope)
- “No data ever stored” (we need nuanced retention/telemetry wording)
- “End-to-end encryption” (define properly; usually “in transit + at rest”)

Safer alternatives:
- “We can provide current compliance posture and third-party reports under NDA where applicable.”
- “Data handling and retention details are documented and available in the Marketplace Security FAQ.”

==============================
6) Marketplace-specific phrasing (AWS/GCP)
==============================
Procurement highlights:
- “Purchase via Marketplace to consolidate vendor spend and streamline invoicing.”
- “Apply purchases to your cloud commitment where applicable (subject to your cloud provider terms).”
- “Start with a committed plan and scale usage with clear metering.”

Onboarding highlights:
- “Marketplace purchase → entitlement activation → link entitlement to your Redwood org in the Console.”
- “Support for multiple cloud accounts and org mapping (with guardrails to prevent mis-linking).”

Avoid:
- Over-promising activation time (“instant”) — better: “typically within X minutes” (need real SLA from Eng/SRE)

Suggested cautious line:
- “Entitlements are usually activated within minutes. If activation is delayed, our support team can help verify provider status and complete org linking.”

==============================
7) SKU naming / taxonomy (copy placeholders)
==============================
Use consistent tier labels across AWS/GCP + Console:
- Redwood Hosted API
- Redwood Dedicated
- Redwood Private
Add-ons (names TBD):
- Compliance Pack (placeholder)
- Extended Observability Retention (placeholder)
- Premium SLA (placeholder)

Copy pattern:
- “Choose Hosted for fastest onboarding. Choose Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. Choose Private for VPC/on-prem requirements.”

==============================
8) Draft FAQ language (customer-facing, not final)
==============================
Q: What happens after I purchase via Marketplace?
A (draft): “After purchase, your cloud provider issues an entitlement. In the Redwood Console, you’ll link that entitlement to your Redwood organization to activate the plan. Once linked, you can create API keys and start sending requests immediately.”

Q: How does Marketplace billing work?
A (draft): “Charges appear on your AWS/GCP bill according to the Marketplace offer you select. Usage and plan details are visible in the Redwood Console.”

Q: Can we use Marketplace spend for an existing Redwood account?
A (draft): “Yes. You can link the Marketplace entitlement to an existing Redwood org, or create a new org during onboarding.”

Q: We have multiple AWS accounts / GCP projects. Can we purchase once?
A (draft): “In most cases, yes—purchase is tied to your Marketplace account, and you can link entitlements to the appropriate Redwood org. If you need multiple entitlements (e.g., separate business units), Redwood Support can help recommend a setup.”

Q: What regions are supported?
A (draft): “Region availability depends on the specific offer and deployment mode. Hosted supports multiple cloud regions; Dedicated/Private are configured during onboarding.”

Q: Can we deploy in our VPC?
A (draft): “Yes, Private deployments can be configured for customer-managed networking (VPC). Contact us to confirm requirements and supported architectures.”

Q: Do you support on-prem or air-gapped?
A (draft): “Private deployments may support on-prem options for regulated workloads. Requirements vary—contact Redwood for validation.”

Q: What data do you store, and for how long?
A (draft): “Data handling depends on configuration and deployment mode. We provide documented options for logging and retention, and you can request our security packet for details.”

Q: Is data used for training?
A (draft, needs policy check): “Customer inputs/outputs are not used to train models by default. Details are available in our data handling documentation.”

Q: What security controls do you support (SSO/SAML, audit logs, encryption)?
A (draft): “We support enterprise authentication options and audit logging features. Encryption in transit and at rest is supported. See the Marketplace Security FAQ for specifics and deployment-mode differences.”

Q: Who do we contact for support?
A (draft): “Use the support contact listed in the Marketplace listing and/or your Redwood support channel. For entitlement activation issues, include your Marketplace entitlement ID and Redwood org ID.”

Q: Can we upgrade/downgrade plans purchased via Marketplace?
A (draft, pending PM policy): “Upgrades are supported; downgrades may take effect at the next billing period depending on provider policies. We’ll document the exact behavior per Marketplace.”

Q: Can we combine Marketplace purchase with a direct contract?
A (draft): “Some customers use Marketplace for standard spend and a direct contract for custom terms. We can advise based on your procurement requirements.”

==============================
9) “Do / Don’t” language reminders (for listing + FAQ)
==============================
DO:
- Emphasize measurable outcomes: latency, throughput, cost controls, reliability
- Emphasize environment flexibility + consistent API
- Say “documentation available” rather than making absolute compliance claims
- Use “supports / provides” instead of “guarantees” unless SLA exists

DON’T:
- Claim certifications or attestations unless GRC confirms current status + scope
- Promise specific activation times without SRE’s thresholds
- Imply we cover the customer’s shared responsibility (esp. Private/on-prem)

==============================
10) Quick snippets for bullets (ready-to-paste candidates)
==============================
Performance bullets:
- “Low-latency inference optimized for real-world traffic patterns.”
- “Cost controls: batching, caching, and routing policies you can tune.”

Ops bullets:
- “Token-level cost and latency visibility in the Console.”
- “Safe rollouts: canary, A/B testing, and automatic fallback options.”

Deployment bullets:
- “Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment options with a consistent API.”
- “Enterprise-ready procurement via AWS/GCP Marketplace.”

==============================
11) Notes to self / next edits
==============================
- Align final wording with the Confluence messaging framework (esp. security phrasing). 
- Confirm with Marcus Lin: what exact claims are allowed in public listing vs only in security packet under NDA.
- Ask Ethan Park / Rafael Mendes: typical entitlement activation latency and how to describe retries + delays.
- Ensure SKU labels match ADR + billing plan codes (avoid “Pro/Enterprise” ambiguity in Marketplace context).
- Add 1–2 short customer-style outcomes (e.g., “reduced p95 latency”, “simplified procurement”), but only if we can back up with a case study or anonymized data.
